headline: Data Center Grid Cost Responsibility
short_summary: This bill directs Dominion Energy Virginia to propose rate changes that allocate costs for increased grid capacity to large energy users, primarily data centers, rather than residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocates, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users.
news_headline: New Virginia legislation shifts data center energy costs
news_summary: Virginia's legislature passed HB 1393, requiring data centers and other large energy users (25 MW or more) to pay for the costs of increasing electric generating capacity. This legislation prevents these costs from being passed on to other customers, aiming to protect residential ratepayers.

headline: Data Center Water Use Transparency
short_summary: This bill requires local water authorities to report the water consumption of data centers, including potable and reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board for public transparency.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (due to increased reporting burden/potential scrutiny).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, SB 553, mandates that local water authorities report data center water usage, which will be aggregated and made available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide transparency regarding the industry's water consumption, a top complaint against data centers.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Regulation
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for high energy use facilities (HEUFs) like data centers, examining sound profiles on nearby residential units and schools, and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Del. Joshua E. Thomas, Del. Sam Rasoul.
opponents: Data center industry, developers (due to increased regulatory burden and potential siting restrictions).
news_headline: Virginia's New Data Center Law: What It Does, Doesn't
news_summary: Virginia's HB 153, which took effect July 1, 2026, mandates that developers of large data centers (100 MW or more) conduct sound studies near homes and schools. While it requires studies and disclosures, it does not set specific noise limits or setbacks, leaving some residents concerned about ongoing noise pollution.
